case_summary: This case concerns whether 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(5)(A), which prohibits unlawful noncitizens from possessing firearms, violates the Second Amendment. The petitioner (United States) argues that unlawful noncitizens are not part of 'the people' protected by the Second Amendment and that the historical tradition of firearms regulation supports disarming those unlawfully present. The respondent argues that 'the people' encompasses all persons with sufficient connections to the United States, including unlawful noncitizens, and that no historical tradition justifies a categorical ban on their firearm possession.
key_legal_issues: Whether unlawful noncitizens are part of 'the people' protected by the Second Amendment
Whether 18 U.S.C. § 922(g)(5)(A) is consistent with the historical tradition of firearms regulation under the Bruen framework
Whether the 'sufficient connections' test from United States v. Verdugo-Urquidez controls the definition of 'the people' across constitutional provisions
Whether historical analogs support categorical disarmament of unlawful noncitizens
Whether the government's interest in public safety justifies restricting Second Amendment rights based on immigration status
